title: Ir: going places and the near future
summary: Voy, vas, va… to say where you go, and ir a + infinitive for what you're going to do.
focus: Conjugation of ir; ir a + place; ir a + infinitive (near future)
content:
## Ir is completely irregular

| | ir (to go) |
|---|---|
| yo | **voy** |
| tú | **vas** |
| él / ella / usted | **va** |
| nosotros/as | **vamos** |
| vosotros/as | **vais** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **van** |

It looks like an *-ar* verb with the stem *v-*. *Vamos* also means *let's go*.

## Going somewhere: ir a

**ir a + place**. Remember **a + el = al**:

- *Voy al cine.* (I'm going to the cinema.)
- *Vamos a la playa.* (We're going to the beach.)
- *¿Vas a casa?* Are you going home? (*casa* takes no article here)
- *Van a Madrid en tren.* (They go to Madrid by train.)

Transport: *en coche, en tren, en autobús, en bici, a pie* (on foot).

## The near future: ir a + infinitive

Like English *going to*:

- *Voy a estudiar esta noche.* (I'm going to study tonight.)
- *¿Qué vas a hacer mañana?* (What are you going to do tomorrow?)
- *Vamos a comer a las dos.* (We're going to eat at two.)
- *No van a venir.* (They aren't going to come.)

Time words that go with it: *mañana, esta tarde, esta noche, el lunes, la semana que viene, el año que viene*.

## Three uses of a

- direction: *Voy **a** Sevilla.*
- near future: *Voy **a** comer.*
- time: *A las ocho.* (At eight.)

bites.title: V is for vamos
bites.rule: Ir doesn't look like ir at all: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van. Think of it as a v- verb with -ar endings, plus that odd voy.
bites.example_meaning: I'm going to the cinema. Are you going too?

bites.title: A + el = al
bites.rule: Spanish won't say 'a el': the two glue together into al. A la stays apart, and casa needs no article at all.
bites.example: Voy al cine y después a la playa.
bites.example_meaning: I'm going to the cinema and then to the beach.

bites.title: Going to = ir a
bites.rule: The near future is ir + a + infinitive, exactly like English 'going to'. Don't drop the a, and keep the second verb in the infinitive.

bites.title: One a, three jobs
bites.rule: Direction (voy a Sevilla), future plans (voy a comer), clock time (a las ocho): one tiny a does all three jobs.
bites.example: Mañana voy a Sevilla a las ocho.
bites.example_meaning: Tomorrow I'm going to Seville at eight.

sorts.title: Which form of ir?
sorts.why: Match the subject: yo voy, tú vas, nosotros vamos, ellos van.

sorts.title: Al, a la or just a?
sorts.why: Masculine el fuses with a into al; la stays separate; casa and city names take a bare a.

sorts.title: A place or a plan?

items.text: Van a comer a las dos.

sorts.why: After ir a, a place means direction; an infinitive means a future plan.

spots.why: Ir a is followed by the infinitive.

spots.sentence: Mis amigos vamos a la playa.
¿Mis padres va a la playa mañana?

spots.why: Ir is irregular: nosotros vamos, never imos.

spots.sentence: ¿Vosotros váis en coche o en tren?
spots.why: Vais is one syllable, so it has no accent.

spots.sentence: Mi madre van al trabajo a pie.
spots.why: Mi madre is one person: va.

realm.content:
## Ir por Eldmark

**Ir** says where you are going (**voy a Emberhold**) and what you are about to do (**voy a subir de nivel**). Proper names take no article: **a Emberhold**, **a Silvermere**; with a mount you ride, without one **vamos a pie**.

vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm going to Emberhold.
Without a mount, we go on foot.

vocabulary.example: Esta noche vamos a hacer una banda.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tonight we're going to do a raid.

vocabulary.example: Mañana voy a subir de nivel.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tomorrow I'm going to level up.

vocabulary.example: La semana que viene vamos a Silvermere.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Next week we're going to Silvermere.
I'm going to buy a mount.

vocabulary.example: Vamos a la banda a las nueve.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We're going to the raid at nine.
We're going to Frostmarch by airship.

bites.title: Ir por Eldmark
bites.rule: Ir says where you're going (voy a Emberhold) and what you're about to do (voy a subir de nivel). Ir a + infinitive is the near future.
bites.example: Mañana voy a comprar una montura.
bites.example_meaning: Tomorrow I'm going to buy a mount.

listening.meaning: Tomorrow we're going to Silvermere on foot.

listening.meaning: Tonight the orc is going to level up.
listening.note: Ir a + infinitive: the near future.

listening.meaning: Are you all going to the dungeon or to the inn?

builds.meaning: Tomorrow I'm going to buy a mount.
We're going to Emberhold by airship.

spots.why: Emberhold has no article: a Emberhold. Al is a + el, only before el.

spots.sentence: Los caballeros va a la mazmorra.

sorts.title: A place or a plan?
sorts.why: Ir a + noun means going somewhere. Ir a + infinitive means going to do something.

quiz.prompt: Mañana yo ___ a comprar una montura.
quiz.explanation: Yo voy: the near future is ir a + infinitive.
Ir a + place. A proper name takes no article, so no al.
hints: Al = a + el, and Emberhold has no el.

meadowbrook.content:
## Ir por el valle

Every day the farmer **va** somewhere: **voy a la mina**, **vamos a la playa a pescar**, **voy al pueblo a pie**. And every plan is **ir a** + verb: **mañana voy a plantar fresas**, **esta noche vamos a la taberna**.

vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm going to the mine.

vocabulary.example: Vamos a la playa a pescar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We're going to the beach to fish.
I'm going to town on foot.
Tomorrow I'm going to plant strawberries.

vocabulary.example: Esta noche vamos a la taberna.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tonight we're going to the tavern.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Next week is the festival.

We're going fishing at the river.

rustwake.content:
## Ir por el páramo

Every trip out of **la cúpula** is **ir a** + place: **voy al mercado**, **vamos a la ciudad en ruinas**, **en caravana** or **a pie**. Every plan is **ir a** + verb: **mañana voy a buscar agua**, **esta noche vamos a escuchar la radio**.

vocabulary.example: Voy al mercado a cambiar tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm going to the market to trade nuts.

vocabulary.example: Mañana vamos al supermercado a buscar latas de comida.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tomorrow we're going to the supermarket to look for cans of food.

vocabulary.example: Voy al trabajo en la cúpula a las ocho.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm going to work in the Dome at eight.
We're going to the town on foot.

vocabulary.example: Mañana voy a explorar el páramo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tomorrow I'm going to explore the plains.

vocabulary.example: Esta noche vamos a escuchar la radio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tonight we're going to listen to the radio.

vocabulary.example: Voy al mercado a cambiar tuercas por agua.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm going to the market to trade nuts for water.

vocabulary.example: Vamos a la ciudad en ruinas en caravana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We're going to the ruined city by caravan.
The traders go by caravan.
Are you going to the plains with your wrist radio?

bites.title: Ir por el páramo
bites.rule: Voy al mercado, vamos a la ciudad en ruinas: ir a + place. Voy a buscar agua, vamos a explorar: ir a + verb is your plan. Remember a + el = al.
